name: Boulder Gap
description: The product nested off-centre in the natural saddle where two weathered granite boulders lean together, real lichen crusts and moss packed into the crevice, cool overcast directional light. Raw inland geology at intimate scale, never a symmetrical pairing.
subject: product
prompt: a heavy faceted glass bottle with a brushed-steel cap, the bottle is the hero of the frame and occupies roughly 60 percent of the frame height, tack-sharp and clearly lit, nested off-centre in the natural saddle where two weathered glacial-erratic granite boulders lean together, the two boulders deliberately unmatched — different sizes, different distances from camera and different heights, never a symmetrical pair with the product centred between them, real mineral banding and quartz veining through the granite, ochre and pale-sage lichen crusts, deep moss packed into the crevice, dark water-staining where runoff tracks down the faces, cool overcast daylight with one soft directional bias from camera-left so the boulder faces separate by tone rather than by hard shadow, a faint warm bounce off the lichen into the shadowed underside of the bottle, a soft out-of-focus rock edge crossing one foreground corner, genuine contact where the bottle rests on stone with a soft occlusion shadow, believable scale between product and boulder, no sunset, no sea, no sky-dominant framing, immaculate commercial clarity
